dedupe_keys.name: room for the river regge reggevisie restoring river dynamics

description: This Climate-ADAPT case study describes the Reggevisie programme on the Regge, a lowland river in the east of the Netherlands that was straightened from 1848 and largely canalised by 1935, leaving wide floods in wet periods and near-stagnant water in droughts. From 2010 the water boards re-meandered stretches of the river, kept part of the canal as a parallel flood channel along the lower and middle Regge, and created room to buffer peak discharges and retain water in dry periods, together with an ecological corridor and recreation. Coverage is the Regge valley in Overijssel. The programme, adopted by the Water Board Regge and Dinkel and continued by Water Board Vechtstromen, runs until 2025 at an estimated total cost of about 25 million euros; the Water Framework Directive and Natura 2000 helped drive it. The page, published in 2016 and updated in 2026, is accessible online as free HTML on the Climate-ADAPT portal with links to project pages and videos. Caveats: benefits for floods and droughts are described, not quantified, and completion was still pending when the page was updated. It illustrates nature-based flood and drought hazard reduction and climate adaptation of river systems; related records are the Isar-Plan, Kruibeke Bazel Rupelmonde and Lower Danube Green Corridor case studies.
name: Room for the River Regge (Reggevisie), restoring river dynamics
outcomes: Re-meandered stretches and a parallel flood channel add buffer capacity for peak flows and retention in droughts, with an ecological corridor, at about EUR 25M.
provider: Climate-ADAPT (European Environment Agency), case study from Water Board Vechtstromen
